messages:
maria: WIP — 'quality sentinel' checklist for quant validation (INT8 / FP8 / GPTQ / AWQ). Short sketch I want feedback on before I turn this into a notebook. TL;DR: pick a small canonical seed pool + edge traps + a matrix of deployment profiles. Paste below.

maria: Items I'm thinking about:
- Canonical seed pool: 4 domains (helpdesk, public QA, code-gen, legal summaries) with 30 seeds each.
- Template suite: short-direct, multi-step, few-shot, chain-of-thought, tabular, constrained-output.
- Edge traps: unanswerable phrasing, long-winded nonsense, numeric precision probes, token-swaps.
- Negative controls: synthetic gibberish + repeated tokens.
- Sampling plan: deterministic reproducible seeds + a small random augmentation pass (paraphrase + typos).
- Metrics: delta-accuracy vs float32 baseline, token-flip-rate, KL divergence on token distributions, p50/p95 latency by profile.
- Profiles: hosted-low-latency, dedicated-high-throughput, private-airgapped (fp8 fallback).

ajay: Nice. Can we include synthetic perturbations (paraphrase + dropout) and latency gates? Also how do you propose weighting domains for a single scalar score?

ben: +1. For weighting I'd do 60/20/20 (core/edge/anti-pattern) if you need a single number (core = helpdesk + public QA). Also add a 'sanity-noise' control: swapped tokens, excessive repetition to catch brittleness.

sofia: Small note on metrics: report both delta-accuracy (vs float32 baseline) and per-case divergence (KL or token-flip rate). Also surface p95 latency and tail memory usage per profile. Keep the regression thresholds explicit.

[eval-bot]: run summary 2029991300: quick sweep (INT8-GPTQ): median delta-accuracy -1.2% on glue-like QA tasks; token-flip-rate 3.8%; p95 latency 120ms (hosted-low-latency). Full logs: s3://redwood-evals/2029/2029991300

maria: Added a 'stress harness' idea: rotation holdouts where we rotate 10% of each domain into holdout every run (prevents overfitting to static seeds). Adversarial traps to stress instruction-following and refusal behavior.

ajay: About the templates — propose we standardize 6 templates and keep 30 seeds each, so 180 instances per domain before augmentations. That keeps runs fast but statistically meaningful.

ben: For seeds, pick the 4 canonical sources I mentioned earlier, then augment with paraphrases+typos at 0.15 noise rate. Also include a small set of long-context examples (>=1024 tokens) to catch kv-cache regressions.

sofia: Deployment profiles again: hosted-low-latency (small batch, KV-cache warm), dedicated-high-throughput (large batch, cold-cache stress), private-airgapped (fp8 fallback path). Tag every result row with profile and quant backend (GPTQ / AWQ / INT8 / FP8).

maria: Proposal for scale: 30 seeds x 6 templates x 4 domains = 720 core instances. Then add ~200 edge traps and ~100 negative controls. Total ~1020 inputs per run — quick to sweep and easy to human-audit. Anyone object to that scale? :rocket:

ajay: Sounds reasonable. Also add a reproducibility artifact: seed file + mapping to dataset IDs and the exact augmentation RNG state.

ben: Do we want human eval tags for ambiguous cases? Quick 3-label scheme (ok / regress / bad) would help triage. Store labels as CSV with sample id and annotator id.

sofia: +1 on human labels. Also propose regression alert thresholds: delta-accuracy <= -2% OR token-flip-rate > 8% OR KL divergence jump > 0.06 triggers a rollback candidate and tags the failing samples for human review.

maria: Great — I'll draft the notebook + a small PR with sampling code and the sentinel checklist doc. Will include the template YAML and a small script to produce the evaluation matrix. Ping me if you want to add template variants. /cc @sofia @ajay
